lowConfidence.claim: Attribution of the 3NF-not-BCNF overlapping-composite-keys condition to Vincent & Srinivasan (1993), IPL 48(6):281–283.
lowConfidence.reason: The mathematical condition is high confidence (verifier's own proof plus exhaustive random check); the paper itself is paywalled and its zbMATH summary is withheld, so the attribution rests on Crossref metadata and Wikipedia's citation of it. Zaniolo (1982) is not cited in the lesson; it concerns elementary-key normal form.

lowConfidence.claim: The extra candidate-key relation in 3NF synthesis comes from later refinements of Bernstein (1976), notably Biskup, Dayal & Bernstein (1979).
lowConfidence.reason: Bernstein 1976 PDF available only as scanned images; Biskup et al. 1979 abstract elided by the publisher. Bibliographic records (Semantic Scholar, bibtex.github.io) and an R implementation citing Bernstein's synthesis with an optional key relation support the wording, which is hedged.

lowConfidence.claim: Lucchesi and Osborn (1978) showed that deciding whether an attribute is prime is NP-complete.
lowConfidence.reason: Original paper paywalled; confirmed by the abstract of Demetrovics & Thi (Acta Cybernetica 11(3), 1994), which states the result and cites Lucchesi & Osborn, plus Crossref metadata for the 1978 JCSS paper.

lowConfidence.claim: Oracle fast-refresh materialised views and SQL Server indexed views maintain results incrementally, with query-shape restrictions.
lowConfidence.reason: Carried from the earlier verified text; not re-fetched in this pass (vendor docs listed in the top-level sources).

analogyReview.scope: All 35 active lessons: 16 analogies added by the authors reviewed for scenario, mapping, stated limit, placement (own blockquote after a blank line), required facts kept outside, and glossary links inside the callout; 19 lessons recorded as not needing one.

rel-th-typed-facts.rationale: Guest list with a host's completeness promise maps to the closed-world assumption; limit (one column, says nothing about attendance) correct.

rel-th-sets-and-sql.rationale: A concrete list of SQL departures from the model; an analogy would add nothing.

rel-th-legal-keys.rationale: Short definitional unit; the employee key table is clearer than a comparison.

rel-th-integrity-rules.rationale: Cloakroom ticket/peg maps to referencing row/foreign-key value/referenced key; refusing to clear a claimed peg = NO ACTION/RESTRICT, voiding tickets = CASCADE; limit names composite, self-referencing and nullable keys. Checked against PostgreSQL 18 constraints docs.

rel-th-data-independence.rationale: Address vs turn-by-turn directions maps to declarative vs navigational access; new bypass = new index; limit says the optimiser may only choose result-equivalent plans over existing access paths.

rel-th-restrict-project-rename.rationale: Notation-introduction unit; the fixture tables show each operator's effect directly.

rel-th-set-operators.rationale: Set operations are familiar from school maths and grounded by the SQL equivalents.

rel-th-products-and-joins.rationale: Every shirt with every pair of trousers = Cartesian product; colour rule = θ; limit correctly says engines need not build the product (hash/merge/index joins).

rel-th-universal-division.rationale: Museum passport: 'no listed museum missing' = double negation; empty list qualifies everyone; limit about who counts as an entrant matches the SQL-vs-algebra candidate difference (verified by execution).

rel-th-equivalent-plans.rationale: Grading fruit before shipping = pushing a one-input selection below the join; limit (cross-input conditions cannot be pushed; optimiser estimates from statistics) matches q11.

rel-th-algebra-limits.rationale: Short list of where algebra and SQL differ; each item is concrete already.

rel-th-dependency-meaning.rationale: Number plate determines model across all sightings = pairwise FD check; limit (plates transfer between vehicles, GOV.UK) correctly motivates adding a date to the determinant.

rel-th-armstrong-inference.rationale: A list of inference rules with a counterexample; the next unit's recipe analogy covers the closure idea.

rel-th-attribute-fixpoint.rationale: Recipes unlocked by available ingredients = firing FDs whose whole left side is known; limit (nothing consumed, order-independent result) is accurate for attribute closure.

rel-th-closure-applications.rationale: Applies the attribute-closure procedure (and its analogy) to a real table; another comparison would repeat it.

rel-th-enumerate-keys.rationale: Procedure with worked examples; the pruning rules are clearer stated directly.

rel-th-minimal-covers.rationale: Short reduction procedure with a worked example.

rel-th-dependency-sql.rationale: Practical SQL behaviour and checks; executable examples are clearer than a comparison.

rel-th-anomalies-and-1nf.rationale: Phone numbers copied onto attendance sheets map to the update, insertion and deletion anomalies; limit distinguishes historical snapshot from copied current fact (consistent with third-normal-test's price-paid warning).

rel-th-second-third-normal.rationale: Continues the shop example and the anomalies analogy from the previous unit.

rel-th-third-normal-test.rationale: Continues the shop example; the quick-diagnosis tip already gives the intuition.

rel-th-bcnf-and-prime.rationale: Single classic example (Teaching) with explicit keys; an analogy would not clarify the prime-attribute exception.

rel-th-safe-decomposition.rationale: Guest-table and table-meal lists joined on table number; 'one menu per table' = shared attribute determines one part; mixed table produces spurious guest-meal pairs. Limit (database cannot notice) correct.

rel-th-decomposition-algorithms.rationale: Algorithm steps with a traced example and a comparison table.

rel-th-independent-facts.rationale: Any drink with any pastry = independent lists (MVD); two short lists = 4NF split; limit (restricted combinations are not independent) correct.

rel-th-measure-and-copy.rationale: Till receipt = historical snapshot, phone contact = cached current value; limit (copies at scale need a built maintenance mechanism) correct.

rel-th-counter-maintenance.rationale: Single shared tally clicker = one hot counter row and its lock; per-gate clickers = sharded counters; limit (locks held until commit; rollback undoes the click) matches PostgreSQL row-locking and the executed rollback test.

rel-th-precomputed-results.rationale: Printed timetable = materialised view as of last refresh; live board = ordinary view; limit (core PostgreSQL recomputes the whole result, no staleness warning) matches the REFRESH docs.

rel-th-analytical-layouts.rationale: The star diagram and named systems are the explanation.

rel-th-copy-consistency.rationale: Mechanism comparison table; the preceding units' analogies cover snapshots, counters and refresh.

rel-th-er-cardinality.rationale: Notation and mapping rules; the crow's-foot table is clearer than a comparison.

rel-th-weak-and-junction.rationale: Flat 3 meaningful only with the block = partial key plus owner key; demolition = ON DELETE CASCADE; limit (key changes must propagate to referencing rows) correct.

rel-th-ternary-facts.rationale: Who brought what to which party: the three true statements correspond exactly to the three Supplies rows and the tempting conclusion to the spurious tuple; limit (only a stated join dependency justifies rebuilding triples) correct.

rel-th-subtype-mappings.rationale: Comparison table of three mappings with executable CHECK.
